campaign: An Act to Amend the Cannabis Legalization Act and the Maine Medical Use of Cannabis Act
firm: unknown. Out-of-state paid circulators were reported
pay: $1 per signature (one circulator, in a recording reported Jan 2026)
deadline: June 8, 2027 filing deadline (for a 2027 election); Feb 2, 2026 was the 2026 cutoff
why: Approved for circulation Dec 8, 2025. In Jan 2026, Secretary Bellows testified that circulators were 'people for hire' shipped in from out of state. A Texas circulator said he was paid $1 per signature. The SOS page still lists it as current, with a June 8, 2027 deadline. Not verified whether signatures were filed for 2026 or whether paid collection continues in Oct 2026.

campaign: Florida Decides Healthcare - Medicaid expansion (2028)
firm: unknown for 2028. For the 2026 drive, The Outreach Team posted paid 'Petitioner' jobs (posted April 8, 2025).
pay: 2026 drive (The Outreach Team, April 2025 posting): $19/hr for circulators, $21-25/hr for leadership, +$1/hr bilingual. The 2028 rate is unknown.
deadline: Feb 1, 2028 (standard Florida deadline for the 2028 ballot; not separately confirmed in sources)
why: Relaunched signature collection for 2028 on Feb 1, 2026. The new model is mail-in petitions (prepaid return envelope) requested through the website, plus 100+ grassroots partners; that model points away from paid field circulation. Brevard's monthly valid count is small (7 in September 2026), which points to low field activity. The group says HB 1205 'dramatically increased petition costs.' It was lead plaintiff in Florida Decides Healthcare v. Byrd. On April 30, 2026, Judge Walker upheld the circulator registration requirement, the out-of-state and non-citizen circulator bans, felon restrictions, the $50,000-per-violation fine and the felony for filling in petition information. Ballot Access News reported the plaintiffs did not plan to appeal (BAN's May 1 post said the ruling would be appealed, so these conflict). The Florida DOS initiative database (constitutionalinitiatives.dos.fl.gov) was blocked by Cloudflare and could not be checked directly.

campaign: Urban Signers LLC - Signature Collector (unnamed petition projects)

deadline: unknown

firm: SignatureDrive.com (Hubschman's firm) would be the natural vendor, but it is not confirmed collecting on these

campaign: Exempts Additional Food Products from State and Local Sales Taxes (SOS #2023 / AG 26-0005)
why: Entered circulation Sept 25, 2026. It is the newest CA statewide initiative in circulation, per the SOS 2026 release index. No funding committee, firm or signature drive activity was found. A proponent with no visible funding is a possible client for a feasibility or full-campaign pitch.

campaign: April 6, 2027 Consolidated Election – nonpartisan/independent nominating petitions and local referenda petitions

campaign: Initiative Petition 26-02: income tax rate 5% to 4% by tax year 2031 (2028 ballot)
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local election officials; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of the Commonwealth

No source found showing that 2028 collection is underway or that a firm has been hired. Hubschman also filed a near-identical version (26-13), which was not certified. This is the most likely well-funded 2028 drive.

Temple failed. This points to a national trend of data-center recalls, a possible service niche.

MNEA money makes this a candidate for a paid drive, but nothing is confirmed. The SOS 2028 petition page could not be fetched (not on the allowlist), so 2028 filing status is unknown.
